title.justification: This title captures the central focus of the paper, which is to enhance the robustness of models against adversarial distributional shifts that occur outside of the training data distribution.

extractions.description: The paper addresses the challenge of adversarial robustness in deep learning by using a domain generalization approach. Specifically, it applies the Risk Extrapolation (REx) method to promote uniform robustness against various adversarial attacks. The method treats different types of adversarial attacks as domains and uses variance-based risk extrapolation to achieve robustness across unseen and seen adversarial perturbations, on datasets like MNIST and CIFAR10. The results show improvements in worst-case adversarial robustness compared to existing baselines.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on enhancing adversarial robustness in machine learning models, which is not directly related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development. The objective is more about improving computational robustness rather than addressing ecological or climate issues.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Adversarial robustness continues to be a major challenge for deep learning. A core issue is that robustness to one type of attack often fails to transfer to other attacks.

applications.justification: The paper focuses on improving the adversarial robustness of machine learning models, which can be applied to various machine learning tasks and industries that require secure and reliable predictive models.
applications.quote: The paper applies the domain generalisation technique of V-REx, which seeks to equalise performance across attacks used at training time.
